references.text: Moses acknowledges that no god can perform such deeds and mighty works as the Lord, reflecting the question 'Who is like you among the gods?'
Describes Jeshurun (Israel) as having a God who is incomparable, who rides on the heavens to help his people
Hannah's song declares that no one is holy like the Lord and that there is no rock like our God
The psalmist asks 'Who is like you, O Lord?' - one who saves the weak from the strong
Praises God's righteousness that reaches to the heavens and asks who is like God, who has done great things
Celebrates God as the one who does wondrous deeds and has revealed his power among the nations
Declares that no one among the gods is like the Lord, and that he alone is God who does wondrous deeds
Asks who in the heavens can be compared with the Lord, and who among the sons of God is like him - a God feared in the council of the holy ones
Calls for praise of God's great and awesome name, for he is holy
Describes God's name as holy and awesome, in connection with his wondrous deeds
The seraphs cry out that the Lord of hosts is holy, holy, holy - emphasizing God's incomparable holiness
The Holy One asks whom he can be compared to or likened to - emphasizing God's incomparability
Declares that no one is like the Lord - he is great and his name is great in power
Asks who is a God like the Lord, who forgives sin - a reflection on God's incomparable character
Moses' song and the Lamb's song praise God for his great and wondrous deeds, asking who should not fear and honor his name, for he alone is holy
The direct allusion to "Who is like you?" links God's saving greatness in Exodus with his faithful nature in the Psalm.
This version is an almost literal reuse of the central theological claim in Exodus 15:11 about God's unique nature.
Revelation's "Who should not fear you?" is a direct theological fulfillment of Exodus' question regarding God's unique holiness and deeds.
